questions.question: Which of the following peaks is at the highest altitude in India?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nanda Devi** is the** second-highest peak in India after Kangchenjunga **(8,586 meters or 28,169 feet), which is located on the border of India and Nepal. However, **Nanda Devi is the highest peak located entirely within India**.
 
• 
 
The mountain is part of the Nanda Devi National Park, which is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site.** The park is known for its **diverse flora and fauna, **including several endangered species such as the snow leopard and the Himalayan musk deer.

 
 
• 
 
The name** "Nanda Devi"** comes from** Hindu mythology,** where Nanda is the name of a** goddess and Devi means "divine" or "goddess"** in Sanskrit. The mountain is considered sacred by the locals and is an important pilgrimage site for Hindus.

 
 
• 
 
**Nanda Devi has two main peaks**, **Nanda Devi East and Nanda Devi West.** The mountain was first climbed in **1936 by a British team led by Bill Tilman and Noel Odell.** Since then, it has been climbed several times by different teams from around the world.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Namcha Barwa **is a mountain located in the** eastern Himalayas**, in the **Tibet Autonomous Region of China**. It has an **elevation of 7,782 meters (25,531 feet)** and is considered one of the most beautiful mountains in the world due to its unique shape and stunning surroundings.

 
 
• **Namcha Barwa** is also known for its challenging climbing routes, and many mountaineers have attempted to reach its summit. However, the mountain's remote location and difficult terrain make it a dangerous climb, and many attempts have been unsuccessful.
 
 
 
• **Kamet is a mountain **located in the** Garhwal region of Uttarakhand state in northern India**. It is the **second-highest mountain peak in the region, with an elevation of 7,756 meters (25,446 feet). **
 
 
• **​**Kamet is part of the **Zanskar Range**, which is a subrange of the Himalayas.
 
 
• Kamet was first climbed in** 1931 by a British expedition led by Frank Smythe.** Since then, it has been climbed numerous times by various expeditions. The mountain is considered a challenging climb due to its height and difficult terrain.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Makalu** is the** fifth highest mountain peak in the world**, located in the **Mahalangur Himalayas range of the Himalayas**.
 
 
• It has an elevation of** 8,485 meters (27,838 feet) **and is situated on the border between **Nepal and Tibet.**
 
• **Makalu** is considered to be one of the most challenging peaks to climb, with technical difficulties and extreme weather conditions making it a formidable climb.
 
• The first successful **ascent of Makalu was made in 1955 **by a French team led by Jean Franco. Since then, numerous climbers have attempted to climb the mountain, with varying degrees of success.

questions.question: This layer of soil is dark in colour as it is rich in humus and minerals. It is generally soft, porous and can retain more water. It is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The layer of soil **you are referring to is called the **topsoil or the A horizon**.
 
• It is typically the **uppermost layer of soil **and is characterized by its high** organic matter content**, which gives it a dark color and rich texture.
 
• This layer is also **rich in nutrients **and is the most important layer for** plant growth.** The **topsoil** is often softer and more porous than deeper layers of soil, which allows for better water retention and root penetration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The B-horizon** typically forms as a result of **weathering** and other** geological processes **that cause **minerals and nutrients** to leach down from the topsoil and accumulate in the **subsoil**.

 
 
• The depth and** composition of the B-horizon** can vary depending on factors such as** climate, parent material, and topography.**
 
 
 
• **Bedrock is a type of solid rock **that forms the** Earth's crust.**
 
 
• It is the layer of **solid rock that underlies soil, sediment, and other unconsolidated material on the Earth's surface**.
 
• Bedrock is formed through the process of lithification, which involves the compaction and cementation of sedimentary materials, or the cooling and solidification of molten rock.
 
 
 
• **The C-horizon is a layer of soil** that is found beneath the **B-horizon** and is characterized by the accumulation of weathered parent material.
 
 
• **This layer **is typically composed of partially **weathered rocks and minerals**, and it is often less developed than the** A and B horizons**.
 
• The** C-horizon** can vary in thickness, depending on the nature of the parent material and the local environmental conditions. 
 
• It is important to note that th**e C-horizon **is not a distinct layer in all soils and may be absent in some soil profiles.
 
• The **C-horizon** is typically not as biologically active as the A and B horizons and has limited nutrient availability for plant growth.

questions.question: What is the main reason behind the substantial rainfall during summer on the western coasts of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Western Ghats**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Western Ghats** are the main reason behind the substantial rainfall during summer on the western coasts of India.
 
• These mountain ranges run parallel to the western coast and act as a barrier to the moisture-laden winds coming from the Arabian Sea.
 
• As these winds ascend the Western Ghats, they cool down, condense, and result in heavy rainfall on the windward side of the mountains.
 
• This phenomenon is known as orographic rainfall and is crucial for the monsoon season in the western coastal regions of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Western Ghats are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity in the world.
 
• They play a significant role in influencing the climate of the region by intercepting the monsoon winds.
 
• The Western Ghats extend from the state of Gujarat in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, covering a distance of about 1,600 km.
 
• They are also home to numerous endemic species of flora and fauna, contributing to their ecological importance.

questions.question: In which of the following states is shifting agriculture locally called Penda?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shifting agriculture**, also known as **slash-and-burn agriculture**, is a farming practice where trees and vegetation are cut down and burned to create fields for cultivation.
 
• In **Andhra Pradesh**, this practice is locally called **Penda**.
 
• This method is commonly used by indigenous and tribal communities in various regions around the world.
 
• **Shifting agriculture** is typically employed in areas with nutrient-poor soils, allowing farmers to use the ash as fertilizer.
 
• After a few years of cultivation, the land is left fallow to recover its fertility, and the community moves to a new area to repeat the process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Orissa**__

 __
 
• In Orissa, shifting agriculture is known as **Podu**.
 
• Podu cultivation is mainly practiced by the tribal communities in the hilly regions of the state.
 
 
 
• **West Bengal**__
 __
 
• In West Bengal, shifting agriculture is referred to as **Jhum** cultivation.
 
• It is commonly practiced by tribal groups in the northeastern parts of the state.
 
 
 
• **Madhya Pradesh**__
 
 
• In Madhya Pradesh, shifting agriculture is known as **Bewar** or **Dahiya**.
 
• This practice is mainly observed in the tribal areas of the state.

questions.question: Which state has the maximum number of Jute mills (as of 2022)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **West Bengal** has the maximum number of jute mills in India as of 2022.
 
• The state is known as the hub of the jute industry in India and contributes significantly to the country's jute production.
 
• Jute mills in West Bengal are primarily located along the banks of the Hooghly River.
 
• The industry provides employment to a large number of people in the state and plays a crucial role in its economy.
 
• West Bengal's favorable climate and soil conditions support the cultivation of jute, which is the raw material for these mills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Jute, also known as the 'Golden Fiber,' is a natural fiber used for making various products like sacks, bags, and ropes.
 
• India is one of the largest producers of jute in the world, with West Bengal being the leading state in its production.
 
• The jute industry in India is regulated by the Jute Corporation of India, which ensures fair prices and quality control.
 
• In addition to West Bengal, states like Assam, Bihar, and Odisha also contribute to the jute industry, but to a lesser extent.
 
• The Indian government has implemented various schemes and policies to support the jute industry, including subsidies and modernization programs.

questions.question: With reference to 'slash and burn' agriculture, which of the following names is NOT related to Odisha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Roca**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Roca** is not a term associated with slash and burn agriculture in Odisha.
 
• Slash and burn agriculture in Odisha is commonly known by names such as **Bringa, Pama Dabi, and Koman**.
 
• This agricultural practice involves clearing forested land by slashing vegetation and burning it to create fields for cultivation.
 
• The ash from the burned vegetation provides nutrients to the soil, which is used for farming until the fertility decreases.
 
• After the soil's fertility wanes, the land is left fallow, and the cycle is repeated on a new plot of land.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Slash and Burn Agriculture**

 
 
• This is a traditional method of agriculture where natural vegetation is cut down and burned as a method of clearing the land for cultivation.
 
• It is also known as **shifting cultivation** due to the shifting nature of crop fields.
 
• Commonly practiced in regions of Latin America, Africa, and Southeast Asia, besides some parts of India.
 
• While it can be sustainable when practiced by small communities with long fallow periods, it can lead to deforestation, soil degradation, and loss of biodiversity when done extensively.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact**
 
 
• Slash and burn agriculture can result in the release of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.
 
• It can also contribute to soil erosion and a loss of soil fertility over time.
 
• Increased deforestation due to this practice can lead to habitat loss for many species.
 
• Efforts are being made globally to find more sustainable agricultural practices to replace slash and burn methods.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Alternatives**
 
 
• Agroforestry: Integrating trees and shrubs into crop and livestock farming systems.
 
• Crop Rotation: Alternating crops in a field to maintain soil fertility and reduce pest and disease problems.
 
• Conservation Agriculture: Techniques such as minimal soil disturbance, maintaining soil cover, and crop diversification.
 
• Organic Farming: Using natural processes and materials for farming to maintain soil health and ecological balance.
